question.text: Which volatility type is used when plugging the current option market price back into the Black-Scholes model to derive the volatility estimate?

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 79 of the source defines implied volatility as the volatility that is reflected in and derived from option prices. Page 80 then describes the reverse-Black-Scholes procedure: given the four observable inputs and the market option price, solve for the volatility — that solved value is the implied volatility. The Trap: Historical, forecasted and realized volatility are computed from price histories or future expectations, not by inverting an option-pricing model against today's market price. Note: The page 79 historical-volatility contrast underscores that IV is the only volatility input not directly observable in the market.
